newsitem.title: USA: AT&T EPS view cut by Salomon, shares tumble.
newsitem.headline: AT&T EPS view cut by Salomon, shares tumble.

text.p: Salomon Brothers anaylst Jack Grubman lowered his 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for AT&T Corp, a move that sparked a selloff in the stock, according to Wall Street traders.
In late morning New York Stock Exchange trade, AT&T shares were off two points to 39-1/2 in active trade.
"It is not only the earnings cuts, but the overall guts of the story," said a trader, referring to the research note.
Grubman was not immediately available to comment or provide detail on the lower forecasts.

Grubman confirmed in a subsequent telephone call to Reuters that he lowered the 1997 earnings estimate to $3.00 per share from $3.60 and the 1998 estimate to $3.25 per share from $3.80, news that was first learned from market sources.
Grubman said his "hold" recommendation on AT&T is unchanged and noted his new estimates may "still be too high."
Fourth quarter 1996 earnings are going to be closer to $0.70 per share than the $0.78 per share he is currently forecasting, he said.
He said the overall reason for the trimmed forecast is greater competition in the telecommunications market.
According to First Call, the 1997 Wall Street consensus earnings estimate for AT&T is $3.68 per share and for 1998 the estimate is $3.48 per share.
The consensus estimate for the 1996 fourth quarter is $0.80 per share.
